rules_evaluated.evidence: Strategy doc M4-in-detail: 'Mood: curious readiness — "I've built enough to try something; let's see what the agent does with it." Stakes back in the room; no compliance framing.' File's own framing matches: L13 'The point: send it off plainly and you find out what you can't steer yet.' Closest-to-violating line is L58 'If the agent stalls, ask it to keep going. The nudge reads as encouragement and lands as a taunt.' — this touches a failure scenario (stall) but stays inside the mood because it's pitched as a craft observation about how nudges land, not a warning about wrongdoing; the file never states an outcome ('not great by design' lives only in the strategy doc, correctly withheld here so M5's read isn't pre-spoiled). Student leaves in a state of watchful curiosity — task sent, hands off, waiting to see — which sets up M5's 'return to the un-packaged run.'

M4's deliberate mood is 'curious readiness' (strategy doc), not 'unease' — rule's precondition ('When module's mood is unease...') doesn't fire. No punitive language present regardless: 'stop it', 'the trace is the evidence either way' (L56) reads as neutral instrumentation, not blame.
